notes: Not written by the 2026-09-28 rotation-accuracy class audit; this records what a real one needs, so the next pass does not start from zero. Holy has no damage priority list to speak of -- Judgement (free as of the paladin-retribution mana-cost fix landed this pass) and Consecration/Holy Strike as baseline filler if forced into melee -- so writing this spec is really about healing, which this rotation format and this engine are not yet set up to model: (1) sim/paladin/holy_shock.go only registers Holy Shock's DAMAGE side (SpellSchool Holy, DefenseType Magic dealt to a target) -- there is no healing cast at all, so even a trivial 'Holy Shock on cooldown, Flash of Light/Holy Light otherwise' priority list would have nothing to point its heal actions at. Flash of Light and Holy Light are not implemented in sim/paladin at all (no flash_of_light.go / holy_light.go); Divine Favor (divine_favor.go) exists as a cooldown but boosts a heal that does not exist yet. (2) The APL system itself already carries what a reactive heal priority would condition on -- APLValueCurrentHealthPercent takes a UnitReference (proto/common.proto's Type enum has Player/AllPlayers by index, not just the caster or the current enemy target), so 'heal whichever party member is lowest' is expressible once heal spells exist. (3) The bigger gap is the encounter side: every ladder/BiS run today is one player being hit by a single dummy target (sim/request's default encounter), which never damages a raid, so there is nothing for a healer's priority list to react to and nothing for a healing sim's own DPS-shaped metrics (this program's HPS/TMI fields already exist on UnitMetrics, unused for paladin) to score meaningfully. Writing Holy for real needs, in order: the heal spells, a raid-damage encounter profile, then the priority list itself -- in that order, since a list with nothing to heal and nothing that hurts is not testable.
